clue.text: Account in newspaper should be this

definitions.text: Account in newspaper should be this

parts.words: Account in newspaper should be this
parts.note: a news report ought to be true rather than invented, so the clue describes what reporting should consist of

explanation.surface: A reader insists that newspaper reports ought to be truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper account should deal in truth, something verifiably real rather than opinion or fiction.

clue.text: Have spare time at first in African city

parts.note: spare means free, as in spare time or free time

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word time

parts.note: to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Someone with a little leisure time goes off to an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue as OWN, FREE, T but are assembled FREE + T + OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Freetown is the capital and largest city of Sierra Leone in West Africa.

clue.text: Say farewell and head for some food

indicators.note: Say tells the solver to speak the following words and write down how they sound

parts.note: ciao is an Italian farewell, and main means head or chief

explanation.surface: A diner says goodbye and heads off for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of fried noodles, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Insurgent arm in quiet Caribbean spot

indicators.note: insurgent means rebellious, so the letters rise up and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: A rebel's weapon lies hidden somewhere quiet in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French island in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Some acclamation for instrument-maker

indicators.note: Some indicates that only part of the following word is wanted, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A violin-maker receives a share of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made celebrated violins in the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: After collapse doctor put on variable spin, with hot air

indicators.note: After places the doctor piece behind the collapse piece
put on means added at the end of what has gone before

parts.note: to collapse is to tumble
Y is a common algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Following a collapse, a doctor adopts a changing political spin full of bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a politician's spin doctor and hot air as empty talk; in fact it is laundry dried by spinning in heated air.
explanation.definitionFit: To tumble-dry clothes is to spin them in a drum through which warm air is blown.

clue.text: Rural town keen to develop computer system

indicators.note: to develop suggests the letters growing into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country town is eager to build up its technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A neural network is a computing system modelled loosely on the connections of brain cells.

clue.text: Parisian who upset clergyman gets a shake

parts.note: qui is French for who, as a Parisian would say

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: REV, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who annoys a vicar is given a shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver is a slight trembling movement, which is a small shake.

clue.text: Boy or girl equally affected by name dropping eave dropping

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Boy or girl equally affected by name dropping eave dropping (6)': the clue is garbled by OCR beyond 'equally affected' (EVENLY anagrammed), the scan is blank and no source gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Boy or girl equally affected by name dropping eave dropping

clue.text: Unusual articles out of the Listener's archive originally

parts.note: ex means out of or from, as in ex-directory
otic means relating to the ear, the organ a listener uses

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of the word archive

explanation.surface: Odd items have been taken from the archive of The Listener magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine, so the capital letter misleads; here a listener is anyone with ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are curious or unusual objects, especially ones of foreign origin.

clue.text: Expected rank first held by churchwarden check toc den

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Expected rank first held by churchwarden check toc den (2,3,8)': the end is garbled by OCR (churchwarden gives PIPE, rank LINE, but the rest is unreadable), the scan is blank and no source gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Expected rank first held by churchwarden check toc den

clue.text: Male office staff touring heart of Turin

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of office

indicators.note: heart of asks for the inner letters of the word Turin

explanation.surface: A man from the office staff goes on a tour of central Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: Male looks like an adjective for the staff but is the definition: a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice is a man's given name, so it is an example of a male.

clue.text: Watch out for this sporting event

definitions.text: Watch out for this sporting event

parts.words: Watch out for this sporting event
parts.note: the warning reads as a caution, but a watch, a timepiece, is what decides this contest, where competitors race the clock

explanation.surface: A warning to look out for an upcoming sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: In a time trial cyclists or drivers race individually against the clock, so the stopwatch decides it.

clue.text: It's absurd copying exercises in a line

indicators.note: in places the exercises piece inside the other letters

parts.note: RY, short for railway, is a line
PE, physical education, means exercises

explanation.surface: Someone mocks people for doing their exercises in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is apish behaviour, foolish imitation of others like a monkey mimicking.

clue.text: Traditional match win edged with confusion

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A traditional contest is won narrowly amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Match suggests a sporting fixture, but here it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A white wedding is a conventional church marriage with the bride in white, a traditional match of two people.

clue.text: One hit boxer, shattering his display minute.

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'One hit boxer, shattering his display minute. (9)': the anagram of I + HIT BOXER is sound but the definition is garbled by OCR, the scan is blank and no source gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: One hit boxer, shattering his display minute.

clue.text: Mastermind maybe succeeded in grilling method

indicators.note: in places the succeeded letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: to grill someone is to quiz them
how means manner or method
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A mastermind perhaps did well with a method of interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running British TV quiz programme with a famous black chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastermind is an example of a television quiz show, hence the maybe.

clue.text: At one time holding Bible classes in centre of Calgary

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an age is a period of time
RE, religious education, is the British school subject covering the Bible
taken as written

indicators.note: centre of asks for the middle letter of the word Calgary

explanation.surface: Someone at one point was running Bible classes in downtown Calgary.
explanation.walkthrough: At one looks like the start of 'At one time' but is the definition, meaning in accord.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at one with someone is to be in agreement or harmony with them.

clue.text: Disheartened lady in shopping centre sounded nervous

indicators.note: in places the shortened lady inside the shopping centre

parts.note: HIGH ST is short for high street, the main shopping street of a British town

indicators.note: Disheartened means losing its heart, so the middle letters of the word lady go

parts.note: a bell that has sounded has rung

explanation.surface: A dispirited woman at the shops sounded anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly strung describes someone tense and easily upset, that is nervous.

clue.text: Live on 50 per cent benefit

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: Someone survives on half their usual welfare payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Benefit suggests a state welfare payment; here it means sake, as in on behalf of.
explanation.definitionFit: Behalf means interest or sake, so acting on someone's behalf is acting for their benefit.

clue.text: After dull run football team climbs table

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not shiny
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: climbs in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: After a bad run of form, a football team rises up the league table.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular table of numbers or other data in rows and columns.

clue.text: Get round course finally, following chap back

indicators.note: following places the final letter after the reversed name
back means the word for the chap is written backwards

parts.note: Dave is a typical man's name, a chap

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word course

explanation.surface: A golfer finishes the course after another fellow returns.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to get round it by avoiding it.

clue.text: Stump sticks out of grass, reportedly, extremely loose

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the sound of the word is written down

parts.note: bamboos are canes cut from bamboo, which is a giant grass

indicators.note: extremely asks for the first and last letters of the word loose

explanation.surface: A cricket stump pokes up out of the grass, said to be very wobbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Stump looks like a cricket stump but is a verb, meaning baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle them, and to bamboozle is to mystify or confuse.

clue.text: Maiden climbs to top of large tree

indicators.note: climbs to top of in a down clue means the letter rises to the front of the word

parts.note: ample means large or plentiful
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl climbs to the top of a big tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broad-leaved tree, famous for its syrup and autumn colour.

clue.text: Boost following express delivery

indicators.note: following places the boost piece after the express piece

parts.note: to express a view is to air it
a boost is a lift, as in a lift to one's spirits

explanation.surface: A boost in sales follows the introduction of express delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Express delivery reads as a single phrase, but express gives AIR and delivery alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift is the delivery of supplies or people by aircraft.

clue.text: Father and I drinking bad hock with cabbage

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the other pieces enclose the jumbled wine

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written

indicators.note: bad suggests spoiled, so the letters of hock are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad and I drink some off white wine with our cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a German white wine from the Rhine, and Pak choi is also known as bok choy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pak choi is a Chinese cabbage with white stalks and dark green leaves.

clue.text: Kid's heading for row, taking in stray dog

parts.note: to kid is to fool, and fox also means to fool; heading for just puts this piece in front

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the row piece surrounds the stray piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to stray is to err, wander from the right path

explanation.surface: A youngster heads for a quarrel while taking in a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid suggests a child and row a quarrel; both are misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox terrier is a breed of small dog originally bred to flush foxes.

clue.text: Hang about with pack of Aussie travellers

indicators.note: about means around, so the droop piece goes round the letter

parts.note: to sag is to hang or droop

explanation.surface: Australian backpackers hang around with their bundles.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia a swag is the bedroll and bundle carried by a swagman, an itinerant worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A swag is the bundle of belongings carried by a tramp or bush traveller in Australia.
